Team —

Quick heads-up: Nimbus Health raised a support ticket this morning reporting a sharp cost spike tied to their /summarize route and a corresponding p90 latency increase. They attached a brief request to our CS thread and sent logs to ops (attached).

Key customer impact:
- 3x token cost increase in a 2-hour window (they estimate ~$4k extra)
- p90 latency on /summarize moved from ~80ms to ~200ms during the same window
- They saw several 5xx errors reported by their own ingestion pipeline, which they traced back to our endpoint timeouts

Ask: can we surface per-route token/cost/latency breakdowns and exception traces in Console within a short timeframe so we can 1) explain to Nimbus what happened and 2) block this from recurring? Concretely I need:
- A dashboard widget that shows tokens/cost/avg/p90 latency by route_id (with filter by model and region)
- A way to link exceptions/5xx traces to the exact route invocation (trace id or request_id)
- An alert rule template (SLO breach + cost spike) we can enable on the customer org

Attachments: nimbus-cost-spike-log.csv (their export)
Related: HubSpot deal 73519 (renewal in ~6 weeks) — prioritize if we can.

I know some of these are roadmap items, so asking for an exception + a quick triage plan. David / Grace: can you give an ETA for an investigation and a minimal Console change we could ship as a hotfix (even a preview flag)? Marissa: can you update Nimbus and keep the renewal owner looped?

Thanks,
Hannah
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

1) Short triage (today) — I will:
   - run a join of our token billing logs with request logs for Nimbus org (route_id + model + request_id) to confirm where cost jump came from

2) Minimal Console hotfix (preview) — technical feasibility: we can expose a per-route aggregation in the Console metrics page that groups by route_id and model. I can prototype a backend rollup query and an API that returns tokens/cost/latency by route. Expect a proof-of-concept by EOD tomorrow if nothing blocking.

3) Tracing -> exceptions linkage — we currently populate request_id and trace_id, but Console doesn't expose a clickable trace view by default. We can add a small button that opens the existing trace UI filtered by trace_id. That should be a low-risk add.

Questions:
- Does Nimbus route all traffic to a single route_id for /summarize? (Marissa: can you confirm)
- Do we want to include token breakdown by prompt vs completion in the initial view? That adds complexity but might help the customer explanation.

I'll take the POC; Grace, can you scope the UX and product requirements for the dashboard tile?

+ a few product thoughts:

- Route identity hygiene: we should encourage (and surfaced in Console) a canonical route_tag that is stable across deployments (so customers don't create many ephemeral route_ids). If Nimbus is using dynamic route ids, per-route aggregation will be noisy. Marissa, can you confirm their integration pattern?

- Metadata model: propose we standardize route metadata to include: customer_provided_route_name, internal_route_id, expected_model, sla_tier. That will make filtering and SLO scoping straightforward.

- Priority: this is customer-impacting and renewal-adjacent. Recommend we mark it P1 for the next 2-week iteration: initial POC for the rollups + an alert template. Full productized Console UX can be roadmap / next cycle.

- Exception tracing: we should make the request_id clickable and show the stack / timeout reason, and surface whether the call was retried by our client. If we add token breakdown by prompt/completion later, we can also show the cost delta contributor.

I can draft the product spec today and push to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/Per-Route+Metrics+Proposal
